A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HouseCrafter and provide readable main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization. A localized table overlap in v2 does not prevent recovering its reported values.

before.justification: v1 reports original 3D-FRONT generation experiments, component ablations, graph-hop sensitivity results, and a 12-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains original 3D-FRONT experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and ARKitScenes results.

M1.justification: v2 introduces fine-tuning with previously generated, noisy reference images and a SEVA adaptation with modified RGB-D channels, positional encoding, and layout attention. Algorithm 1 changes from depth-first pose-graph traversal to breadth-first location-graph traversal, with room and doorway connectivity. The floorplan geometric features are also revised. v1's explicit object-centric post-refinement stage is no longer included in the described pipeline.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic 3D-FRONT scenes. v2 retains that coverage and adds fine-tuning and evaluation on real-world ARKitScenes, including Table 7 and Figure 16. This introduces real sensor data, noisy depth, and constrained camera trajectories; it is an adapted, fine-tuned model rather than a demonstrated zero-shot transfer.

E2.justification: v2 adds BlockFusion, textured using Meshy, to the quantitative, qualitative, and human comparisons alongside retained CC3D and Text2Room. It also evaluates a monocular-depth alternative using UniDepth and an object-token floorplan-encoding alternative, and separately compares CaPE with DeCaPE. These materially expand the evaluated comparison methods beyond v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds connected-component counts for mesh artifacts and an A6000 runtime protocol that includes rendering 40 images for CC3D. The sensitivity experiment changes from varying graph-hop thresholds with FID/mAP to regrouping locations and varying view counts with FID/PSNR. The original 3D-FRONT split and three-reference/three-target ablation setup remain. The expanded user study retains an unexplained total of 228 responses.

E4.justification: New analyses isolate DeCaPE, examine autoregressive error accumulation and noisy-reference fine-tuning, compare generated versus monocular-estimated depth, and test alternative floorplan encoding. v2 also adds visual RGB-only failure examples. The original hop-distance analysis is replaced by a view-count study, while v1's post-refinement demonstration is removed.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without uncertainty measures. v2 Table 4 introduces plus/minus quantities for runtime and image/block counts, such as HouseCrafter's 24 ± 10 minutes. The dispersion measure and underlying sample counts are unspecified. Neither version provides systematic repeated-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes HouseCrafter's IS/mAP from 4.24/46.48 to 4.37/45.77 and adds BlockFusion and artifact-count results. Matching v1's full-model variant ⑤ to v2's ⑥ reveals FID changing from 16.70 to 17.75, although v2 Table 6 still reports 16.70. New entries cover fine-tuning, depth/layout alternatives, runtime, and ARKitScenes. These are revised or additional results, not established same-setting improvements across versions.

T1.justification: The floorplan feature definition changes from ray depth and height above the floor in v1 to projected-ray depth and ray–floor angle in v2 Section 3.2.2. The CaPE/DeCaPE attention identities, invariance reasoning, and consistency-metric formulas otherwise remain. v2 additionally makes the existing CaPE transform explicit as a block-diagonal matrix; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about floorplan-guided, consistent RGB-D generation and house-scale mesh reconstruction remain. v2 removes the conclusion's blanket assertion that previous approaches could generate only room-scale scenes and qualifies its positioning around text or 2D-layout guidance, while acknowledging house-scale generation using 3D layouts.

C2.justification: v2 explains autoregressive error accumulation, motivates noisy-reference fine-tuning, and discusses the appearance-versus-depth tradeoff of alternative floorplan encoding. It adds real-data challenges and changes the limitations discussion toward joint generation/reconstruction and unsuccessful SuGaR reconstruction trials. v1's specific discussion of baked-in lighting and redundant views is removed; the limitation concerning missing object-instance information remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents depth clipping to 0–3 meters, channel averaging during decoding, camera sampling and room-graph construction, noisy-reference data preparation, SEVA integration, and runtime measurement details. Original base-training hyperparameters are retained. v1's post-refinement recipe and project-page link disappear, while both versions still promise code and weights. Fine-tuning budgets and ARKitScenes split/sample details remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The related-work framework is retained, with a focused expansion discussing SceneCraft's house-scale generation and contrasting 3D proxies with 2D floorplans. New references include SEVA, ARKitScenes, SuGaR, GTA, and additional scene-layout methods. Publication updates and consolidation of duplicate latent-diffusion references do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and method exposition, moves autoregressive generation into the overview, divides the generation module into numbered subsections, and reorganizes the appendices into a numbered supplement with a contents list. Terminology and explanatory passages are revised throughout; author order and equal-contribution notation also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, replaces the teaser, adds pipeline and graph-construction illustrations, redraws floorplan encoding, and expands comparison panels. v1's separate layout-ablation table is incorporated into v2 Table 2; additional tables and diagnostic figures are introduced. The user-study interface is retained and relocated. v2 Table 7 visibly overlaps adjacent text.

improvement.justification: The new component comparisons and explicit analysis of autoregressive error accumulation provide useful support for design choices that v1 did not isolate, while expanded implementation explanations improve understanding. These gains are limited by inconsistent full-model FIDs in Tables 2 and 6, an unreconciled user-study total after adding BlockFusion, sparse ARKitScenes protocol details, and the overlapping Table 7 layout. The revision therefore supports a qualified quality improvement rather than an unambiguous substantial one.
